journeys.lead: You type the organisation's name. Sutra, the organisation's helper (the code calls it Root), asks you what you want to create until it is clear, decides the department itself, builds it with its five functions from the template that fits, hands your words over and tells you. No stamp at birth. J1 ends there: what the department does with your words is its own life, J2.

journeys.title: The five functions work toward the identity's goal

steps.text: The department's Identity looks at the identity Root stamped: is it good enough to start on? If not, it asks questions until it meets its own standard; then the department starts.

steps.text: Priority answers from the budget and the present work: grant, refuse, or counter. Adaptation accepts or changes its proposal. The exchange is on the department's one board and is bounded: four hops, fifteen minutes, its spend.
steps.code: priority.read, priority.bargain, priority.post; the board's thread bounds (engine page, section 5)

steps.text: If they cannot agree, or the limit is hit, it goes to Identity, which closes it against the goal and the rules. What Identity cannot settle goes to you as an ask.
steps.code: today the limit's default is refuse and nothing goes up; the alarm to Identity exists for a run past its window

steps.text: A granted workflow goes to Root, which checks it against Sutra's standards and registers it on the department's record. It does not go into the Library.
steps.code: today the runtime's validate checks and born_template writes the record home's Library (S-25 changes both)

Audit reads what was filed against the identity; a finding goes to Identity.

Adaptation senses how far the goal is and proposes the next move: back to step 2. The loop ends on one check: does the identity's done-when now hold? Audit's reading in step 7 answers it. When it holds, Identity tells you the goal is reached and Adaptation stops proposing.

journeys.lead: J1 ends with the department made and its identity stamped by Root: the goal, the rules, done when. J2 is the department's life: Adaptation proposes what to do next, Priority answers from the budget and the present work, Identity closes a conflict between them, and you close what Identity cannot. What is granted runs; Audit reads the result against the identity; the loop goes on until the goal holds. Identity speaks to you throughout: beside every step, it tells you what was made, and asks only when a rule says ask; no other function speaks to you.

steps.text: The department's Identity files your words as the Brief; the first engine wakes on it. What goes outside asks you first only if a rule says so, or if the born rule about the first publish stands (your open call, J2 step 6).
Every 3 s the motor asks Coordination who goes first; one run per department per tick.
Plan is ready: a Brief version it has not run on. Its blockers run in order: no engine ask pending; Identity's gate; Priority's envelope; the chain under 12.
Plan runs: read the Brief (code), propose the pages (model), fit (code), file the Site plan v1 with its check. The chat shows "Plan is working: …".

Check wakes on the Pages: lists the stamped rules that apply (code); reads each page against them (model, only when there are any); builds; Build v1 with its check.

Adaptation wakes on the checked Live site: senses, reads the ladder, proposes a step's move up to Priority; granted, to you as a rung ask.

journeys.tag: THE FLOW YOU WANT · from the recorded thesis (Beer's five; the board) · each step says built or to build
said: Identity has to be stamped by the root. Once identity is good enough, then the department starts. If, at times, it happens that the identity is not good enough, then identity will ask questions of itself to reach its standards. Once it's done, how will the workflow look between these 5 functions to reach the goal of the identity? I think that is the journey.
I think the original thesis was that adaptation and priority work with each other, and if there is a conflict, then I need to resolve it somewhere. That is how we have designed it.
2 to 5 workflows, there is no limit to that.
Keep it simple for now the way you have written. We can always evolve it later on.
The high level makes sense, though all nine steps, the ninth step is not clear. The first eight steps are clear.
For now, you can just keep these eight journeys and go with this. For the detailing of these journeys, you can do it later on.
2026-10-01, on J2.a: “I think knowing the identity is good enough. We need to define identity and its journeys.”

2026-10-01, on J2.b: “Deciding what to do next: first, workflow from the library template or automation from identity. Default is a template if there is one, but if there is no template, then how do we solve for it? What's the process of adaptation for doing that? I want to focus on that. There, I want to take identities and goals, and use how much logic, considering various practices, is in place. This is the shape, and other various ways to create workflows and logic will come. There, I want to go deeper into it.”
journeys.today: The website template's line as built: a Brief filed by Identity wakes Plan, then Write (one call a page), Check (against stamped rules), Publish (held for the first-publish stamp), then Live site; Audit and Adaptation wake on the checked site. The organic kind (v2.306.21): Adaptation shapes the whole line from the first words, one stamp births it. The earlier rows of this journey are kept in the data file under was. Source: line.md, engines-and-library.md.
sub: Identity checks what Root stamped, asks until it meets its standard, then starts the department. Founder 2026-10-01: knowing the identity is good enough; Identity and its journeys are to define (needs to be filled).

Adaptation reads the identity and makes the workflows: from the Library or its own. This is where workflows are created. Founder 2026-10-01: a template if there is one; with no template, Adaptation makes the workflow from the identity, the goal and the practices in place; that process is the focus (needs to be filled).
Adaptation proposes; Priority answers grant, refuse, counter; bounded.
They cannot agree: Identity closes it; what it cannot settle comes to you.
A granted workflow meets the standards or is sent back; registered on the record.
Coordination gives one workflow its turn; it runs step by step, AI inside, code around; it files what it made; the envelope holds it.
Coordination: who goes first · Priority: the envelope · one workflow's own run: not drawn yet

Audit samples, checks, judges against the identity and files a finding. Identity weighs it three ways: a missing fact only you know becomes a question to you; a wrong that needs your yes becomes an ask; anything else goes back to Adaptation as the next thing to do.
Adaptation senses the gap and proposes again, or learns, crystallizes, grows; when done-when holds, Identity says so.

journeys.title: Words after go-live: a change, a question, a correction, an idea

steps.text: You speak: on Root's chat with the department's chip, or inside the department, or in a function's chat.
On Root the words are handed on as a post from Root to the department's Identity; the answers come back onto Root's board, marked via Root.
The department's Identity reads (code) and recognises the journey: task, query, directive, feedback, new-idea.

Task: the take gives go / ask / refuse, what you are unsure of, a rule your words state, thin. Go files a Brief version and tells "filed in the Brief"; the line runs from Write on; Publish needs no second stamp.
Query: answered from the record's lines: the plan, the site, version counts, what waits, the latest text filed.
Directive: restated as one rule with a tag and a scope: J4.
Feedback: the page, what changes now, a rule to carry; the correction filed to the line and marked against the step that made the page.
New idea: to Adaptation: J5.
The function's chat keeps your words said to it, the tells of the line on the Brief versions they made, and its own thinking as quiet lines.

rulings.words: Verification as a product (founder, 2026-10-01, verbatim kept): “A goal is an outcome which we want... a goal is creating a reality, right? Something in reality you're trying to create... That reality should be articulated enough so that an LLM can test it against it. It has to be articulated from various angles from an LLM point of view, and that verification engine is very important here.” “There are various levels of abstraction in terms of a goal, so we need to have various levels of abstraction coded up. Depending on the level of abstraction, we need to have a standardized template which we think really works in verification level.” “I think this is verification logic as a whole product... one of those products of the root, which is like a template.” “That kind of verification is used by audit as well at a workflow level. It is also used at a work item level.” “When we break down the task into various dimensions, the verification for each dimension is created. At the end of it... one verification should work, which includes all kinds of verification from a design point of view, a product point of view, and a strategy point of view. Otherwise, we need to have a rework there.” “There are three components of the workflows. Those three components need to speak to each other as well to align to a common thing. There is also an open problem statement... Linear is one way, but I don't want to solve by the way because that doesn't work.” “Don't miss out on anything.” STRUCTURE (Claude, for the founder's marks): (1) four levels of a goal: direction (no number; frames), target (a metric, a number, a date, a source; verified by a reading from a measuring workflow), outcome (an artifact meeting a specification written from several angles; one check per angle plus one combined judgement), atom (one step's output and its own check); only outcome and atom end a workflow. (2) the angles for a website: product, design, tech, content, strategy (content added by Claude; the founder named design, product, tech, strategy). (3) the components of one verification: subject, claim, evidence, method (code, LLM, person), verdict, severity. (4) the verification engine is a workflow of its own: input the artifact and its specification, output a verdict artifact, run by Audit at workflow level and at atom level. (5) specification standards: per outcome kind, published standards are the starting template (placeholder until named). (6) the three components of a workflow: goal as specification, work as atoms, verification; aligned by a trace (every verify line to a specification line; every atom's output to a verify line); Claude's reading, to confirm. (7) the open problem statement: a goal whose reality cannot yet be written; a probing workflow comes first and its output is the specification (the how ladder: find, derive, synthesise). (8) the ways: verification first; by dimension then integrate; iterate (bounded rework); probe; linear only when the how is known. For a website in v1: verification first, by dimension, iterate. (9) where it sits: the templates are Root's standards; Adaptation's Make reads them first; Audit runs them; Identity's done-when is written at the target level; the compass guides how, the templates say what counts as done.
rulings.status: ruled; marks owed on the four levels, the five angles, the v1 way and the three components
rulings.contradiction: the website kind's Check today verifies only stamped rules and pages_have_html; Audit judges facts only; no specification template exists per outcome kind; Root holds no verification template; the first-publish check is 'has_index_html'

rulings.words: The PRD's structure (founder, 2026-10-01, verbatim): “The six families don't make sense right now, so let's use what we can use from that, and let's create the structure. Let's go with the structure which we have created.” Earlier the same day: “These four structures are not connecting with each other. They are not part of some structure which I chose.” “Maybe we don't need to grow into that many axes, which are not required, but as and when we have a new idea, can we make sure that we modify the current axes?” RULED: one structure, a system of the same shape at every level; three faces (PARTS what it is made of, LIFE what it does over time, MEETINGS how a person meets it); six levels (organisation, department, function, engine, workflow, atom); every idea gets a card (THIS IS, ONE OF level x face, WORK ON, BECAUSE) and one cell; the kind is found, not picked; the axes change only when an idea needs it. The six families stay the compass a department holds (Adaptation's how methodology), not the faces. Page: platform/structure.html.
rulings.contradiction: the sidebar and the function pages' renderer still carry older words (objects, templates); the older-word pages (the model, type system, builders, bootstrap, what comes first) keep their cells until folded; nothing in the code knows the structure
